svg.title: Food unavailability changes hunger circuitry early
svg.desc: Figure 8, a three-panel schematic of a mouse study. A: matched automated feeder scenes show a nose poke delivering a pellet when food is available and an empty cup when delivery is withheld. AgRP activity decreases before rewarded pokes and increases after unrewarded pokes. B: PVH neurons expressing Sim2 provide excitatory input to arcuate AgRP neurons. C: a separate food-removal experiment begins at lights-out. Both schematic curves represent fasting; the AgRP population calcium signal rises more slowly when PVH-Sim2 neurons are inhibited. A separate blood assay at one hour found no significant changes in ghrelin, insulin, or leptin. The drawing illustrates the early fasting response qualitatively.
svg.text: Food unavailability changes hunger circuitry early

g.text: Mice at a previously reliable automated feeder
AgRP activity rises after unrewarded pokes
